title: In vitro enzymatic activity assay for ENOLASE in mammalian cells in culture
protocol: Grow mammalian cells under conventional conditions until around 90% confluence in 10-cm dishes.
Wash the cells once with PBS.
Add 0.5 mL of lysis buffer to the cells (RIPA or NP-40 buffer may be used).
Scrape the cells and transfer them into 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes.
Break the cells by sonication.
Centrifuge the lysate at 20,000g for 30 minutes to clear it.
Determine protein concentration spectrophotometrically using the Bradford method (Biorad #500-0006).
Freeze samples at -80°C until further analysis.
Prepare two buffers: reaction buffer without 2PG and reaction buffer with 2X (4.5 mM) 2PG for assay procedure.
Equalize biological samples for protein concentration.
Pre-mix samples at dilutions from 1:500 to 1:10 with reaction buffer A.
Prepare a negative control set by adding 2 µM PhAH to samples.
Use mammalian blood diluted 1:1 with lysis buffer, sonicated, and centrifuged at 20,000g as a positive control.
Aliquot 100 μL of each sample into black-walled, clear-bottom 96 well plates.
Include wells without added biological specimen (100 μL buffer A alone) as negative controls.
Start the reaction by adding 100 μL of Buffer B to initiate the enolase substrate reaction.
Record fluorescence readings every 30 seconds (NADH excitation 360nm, emission 460nm).
Determine the slope of the time-dependent decrease in NADH fluorescence for each sample.
Subtract the slope of the negative control to account for background drift and non-Enolase mediated oxidation of NADH.
Express relative enolase activity as relative fluorescent units/mg protein or as a ratio of the average of all samples if protein loading was equalized.
Prepare fresh reaction buffer and aliquot 0.9 mL in a 1 mL cuvette.
Monitor the absorbance at 340 nm until reading is constant.
Add 0.1 mL of sample to the cuvette and mix thoroughly by pipetting up and down.
Use 0.1 mL of lysis buffer for the blank.
Record the reduction in absorbance for about 5 min.
Measure the slope of the linear curve (change in absorbance/min).
Calculate enzymatic activity using the equation provided.
